Terms of Service

IMPORTANT — NOT AN EMERGENCY SERVICE
TraceTheBreak is not an emergency service. Do not use this app to report immediate hazards, life-threatening situations, or active emergencies (for example, a downed power line, a gas leak, or a severe road hazard). In an emergency, contact your local emergency service or the relevant utility's emergency hotline directly. We do not monitor reports in real time and cannot guarantee anyone will see or act on a report quickly.

1. Operator
TraceTheBreak ("the App") is an independent, community-run project built and maintained by volunteers around the world. It isn't operated by a single registered company — "we", "us", and "our" refer to the people who contribute their time to keep the project running.
For questions about these Terms, contact us at contact@tracethestuff.com.

2. About TraceTheBreak
TraceTheBreak is a community platform that lets you:
- report local infrastructure problems, including but not limited to water, electricity, sewage, gas, heating, roads, streetlights, waste management, telecommunications, and similar public issues;
- view and track the status of reports;
- share reports with the relevant municipality, utility company, or other responsible authority;
- view community-submitted weather and wind observations;
- view publicly available environmental and air-quality information;
- explore reports and observations on an interactive map.
TraceTheBreak is meant to improve communication between residents and public service providers. It does not replace emergency services — see the notice above.

3. Eligibility and Accounts
You must be at least 16 years old to use the App.
You may create an account using Google Sign-In or another supported authentication provider.
You agree to provide accurate account information, keep your account secure, and remain responsible for all activity performed using it. You're responsible for keeping your login credentials confidential.

4. Your Content
You keep ownership of all reports, comments, photographs, and other content you submit.
By submitting content, you grant us a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to store it, display it within the App, distribute it to other users, send it to the relevant municipality, utility company, or public authority so the issue can be resolved, and make reasonable technical modifications (such as resizing an image or converting its format).
You confirm that your submissions are accurate to the best of your knowledge, that you own the content or have permission to share it, and that it doesn't infringe anyone else's rights.
Where avoidable, don't include another person's personally identifiable information in a report — for example, faces, license plates, or house/apartment numbers not relevant to the issue. We may edit, blur, or redact part of a report's text or images to protect a third party's privacy, without removing the underlying report.

5. Public Reports
Infrastructure reports are meant to be publicly visible. Depending on your privacy settings, a report may display your username or an anonymous identifier, its category, description, photographs, status, submission date, and coordinates.
The reported location itself is always public, since it's the point of the report and can't be anonymized without making the report unusable.

6. Anonymous Weather Observations
Wind, atmospheric pressure, and similar weather observations submitted through the weather-tracking feature are stored separately from user accounts and are meant to be anonymous. We make reasonable efforts to keep it that way, though absolute anonymity can't be guaranteed for technical logs kept for security and operational purposes.

7. Municipal Administrators
Certain municipalities or regions have designated administrators, who may review reports, update their status, communicate with users through the app, flag duplicate, abusive, or invalid reports, and manage reports within their assigned jurisdiction, accessing the limited account information necessary to do so.
Administrators act independently for the substance of their decisions; we don't guarantee the speed, accuracy, or completeness of any admin's review, status change, or resolution of a report. If an issue is safety-critical, follow the emergency notice above rather than relying on admin action.

8. Acceptable Use
You agree not to: submit knowingly false or misleading reports; intentionally submit duplicate reports to spam the platform; upload illegal, abusive, threatening, defamatory, or discriminatory content; upload photographs that violate another person's privacy or rights; impersonate another person, organization, or authority; interfere with the App's security or operation; attempt unauthorized access to accounts or systems; misuse bots, automated tools, or scraping; or use the App in a way that could endanger public safety.
We reserve the right to remove content that violates these Terms.

9. Report Accuracy
Reports reflect the opinions and observations of the users who submit them. We don't verify every report before publication. Evaluate information independently before relying on it, especially anything safety-related.

10. Suspension and Termination
We may suspend, restrict, or permanently terminate an account that violates these Terms, repeatedly submits false or abusive reports, misuses platform features, or threatens the safety or integrity of the community — with or without prior notice depending on severity.

11. Third-Party Services
TraceTheBreak relies on outside providers, including Google (sign-in), Supabase (authentication, database, hosting, storage), OpenStreetMap and its Nominatim service (maps, place search, geocoding), OSRM-based routing services, and Resend (transactional emails). These providers operate under their own terms and privacy policies, and we're not responsible for interruptions or failures caused by them.
Map data is © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL). Weather and air-quality data shown in the app come from open public feeds and user submissions; we don't guarantee their uptime, accuracy, or real-time precision.

12. Availability
We aim to keep TraceTheBreak available at all times but don't guarantee uninterrupted service. Maintenance, technical failures, internet outages, or third-party disruptions may temporarily affect availability.

13. No Warranty
TraceTheBreak is provided "as is" and "as available." To the maximum extent permitted by law, we disclaim all warranties, express or implied, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, non-infringement, and accuracy or completeness of information. We don't guarantee that reports will be reviewed, that municipalities will respond, that infrastructure issues will be resolved, or that environmental or weather data is accurate or current.

14. Limitation of Liability
To the fullest extent permitted by law, we're not liable for indirect, incidental, consequential, special, or punitive damages arising from your use of (or inability to use) the App, reliance on any report or environmental information, decisions made by municipalities or public authorities, or actions taken by other users.
Since TraceTheBreak is free to use, our total liability is limited to the minimum amount permitted by applicable law.

15. Indemnification
You agree to indemnify and hold harmless TraceTheBreak's contributors, administrators, and service providers from claims, damages, liabilities, and expenses arising from your use of the App or your violation of these Terms.

16. Intellectual Property
The App itself — its software, design, logos, graphics, and original content (excluding user submissions) — is protected by applicable intellectual property law. You may not copy, modify, reverse-engineer, or redistribute any part of it except as permitted by law.

17. Changes to These Terms
We may update these Terms from time to time. Material changes will be announced within the App or by other reasonable means. Continuing to use TraceTheBreak after updated Terms take effect means you accept them.

18. Governing Law
Because TraceTheBreak isn't operated by a single registered company, we apply the laws of to interpret these Terms, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. Disputes are subject to the competent courts of that jurisdiction, unless mandatory law says otherwise.

19. Severability
If any part of these Terms is found invalid or unenforceable, the rest remains in full force and effect.

20. Contact
Questions about these Terms can be sent to contact@tracethestuff.com. If your question relates to your account, please include your in-app username so we can find it and respond.
privacy_policy:
Last updated: July 31, 2026

Privacy Policy

IMPORTANT — NOT AN EMERGENCY SERVICE
TraceTheBreak is not an emergency service. Do not use this app to report immediate hazards, life-threatening situations, or active emergencies (for example, a downed power line, a gas leak, or a severe road hazard). In an emergency, contact your local emergency service or the relevant utility's emergency hotline directly. We do not monitor reports in real time and cannot guarantee anyone will see or act on a report quickly.

1. Operator
TraceTheBreak ("the App") is an independent, community-run project built and maintained by volunteers around the world. It isn't operated by a single registered company — "we", "us", and "our" refer to the people who contribute their time to keep the project running.
For questions about these Terms, contact us at contact@tracethestuff.com.

2. Data we collect
- Account data: when you sign in with Google we receive your name, email address, and profile picture from Google, which we store as your username, avatar, and Google account link. If you're given moderator/admin access, we also store your admin level and the country/municipality you're responsible for.
- Reports and content: the category, description, priority, and precise coordinates of any issue you report; any photos you attach (initial, "in progress," and "fixed" photos); votes you cast on a report's status; and, if you delete your own report, the reason you give for deleting it.
- Location: the coordinates you submit with a report (required — this is the point of the report), and, separately, your approximate device location if you allow the app to use it to center the map near you. We do not store a history of your movements — only the coordinates attached to reports you actually submit.
- Engagement data: contribution points, reputation tier, streaks, and quest/badge progress generated from your activity in the app.
- In-app notifications: messages sent to you (e.g. status updates on your reports) and, if you're an admin, messages you send to other users.
- Anonymous data: wind speed/direction/pressure observations submitted through the storm-tracking feature, and general "bump" location pings, are not linked to your account or any other personal data.
- Device preferences: theme, language, and similar display preferences are stored only in your browser's local storage, not on our servers.

3. Legal basis for processing (EU/EEA users)
- Contractual necessity: account data, report content, and coordinates needed to deliver the app's core reporting and mapping functionality.
- Legitimate interests: detecting and preventing abuse or spam, keeping leaderboard/engagement data reliable, and routing reports to the relevant municipal admin or utility company.
- Consent: access to your device's precise location (requested via a browser/OS permission prompt you can decline or revoke at any time), and any non-essential email such as periodic recap or digest emails, which you can opt out of.

4. How we use it
To operate the map and reporting features; to route your report to the right municipality or utility company and let them know about it; to show admins the reports in their jurisdiction; to run the app's streaks/quests features; to send you notifications and, if you opt in, periodic recap emails; and to moderate abuse (e.g. reviewing flagged reports or photos, or restricting accounts that violate our Terms of Service).

5. Photos and image metadata
Photos you upload through the app are automatically re-encoded on your device before upload (resized and recompressed), which strips embedded EXIF metadata such as GPS coordinates, camera model, and precise capture time. We do not receive or store that metadata.

6. Who we share it with
- Utility companies and municipal admins: report details (including your report location, photos, and — unless you've hidden it — your username) may be shared with the relevant utility company or municipal admin so the issue can be addressed.
- Service providers we use to run the app: Google (sign-in), Supabase (hosting, database, authentication, and file storage — hosted in the EU), OpenStreetMap/Nominatim (map tiles, place search, and reverse-geocoding of report coordinates into a readable location name), an OSRM-based routing service (turn-by-turn directions, if you use that feature), and Resend (sending transactional and digest emails).
- We do not sell your personal data, and we do not share it with advertisers.

7. Public visibility
Report details, their location, status, category, and any attached photos are visible to anyone using the app. Your username is shown alongside your reports by default; you can hide this in Settings, and a short anonymous ID will be shown instead. Community leaderboard and quest-completion feeds may show your username and points if that setting is on.

8. Cookies and local storage
We do not use tracking cookies or third-party advertising cookies or pixels. We use your browser's Local Storage only for strictly necessary, on-device preferences — such as UI theme, language, and session/authentication tokens needed to keep you signed in.

9. Data retention
We keep your account and report data for as long as your account is active. If you request account deletion, we permanently erase your personal account details (email, name, avatar, and the account's link to you). Public reports you submitted remain visible on the map — since they document a real infrastructure issue relevant to other residents and to municipal record-keeping — but are permanently disassociated from your identity and are shown as submitted by a deleted/anonymous user. We may also retain certain records (such as anonymized logs used to prevent abuse of the notification system) for a limited period after deletion.

10. Your rights
Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, export, or delete your personal data, and to object to or restrict certain processing. You can update your username, avatar, language, and username-visibility setting directly in the app, delete your own reports at any time, and request full account deletion by contacting us at contact@tracethestuff.com. If you believe we haven't handled your data properly, you also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority.

11. Children
TraceTheBreak is not directed at children under 16, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.

12. Security
We rely on our infrastructure provider's access controls and encryption in transit to protect your data, and restrict admin-level access to information based on role and assigned jurisdiction.

13. International data transfers
Our database and file storage are hosted in the EU (Ireland). Some of the outside services we use (such as Google and Resend) may process data outside the EU/EEA; where that happens, we rely on the safeguards those providers offer (such as Standard Contractual Clauses).

14. Changes to this policy
We may update this policy from time to time; the "Last updated" date above will reflect the most recent change. Continued use of the app after an update means you accept the revised policy.

15. Contact
Questions about Privacy Policy can be sent to contact@tracethestuff.com. If your question relates to your account, please include your in-app username so we can find it and respond.
